issues.failure_explanation: Figure 2 illustrates the Example-2 Dirichlet BVP with three trefoil-shaped holes, and the caption asserts the computed solution has error less than 1e-13. The text reporting exactly these trefoil experiments states E = 4.2995e-8 and E = 4.2994e-8; the 1e-13 accuracy belongs to the circular-hole computation of Figure 3 (E = 2.0323e-13 and 2.0275e-13). The caption thus overstates, by about five orders of magnitude, the accuracy the paper establishes for irregularly shaped holes.

failure_location.quote: The error of the computed solution is less than $10^{-13}$, away from a small neighborhood of the boundary. See Section~\ref{sec: dirichlet num} Example 2 for details.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the caption to the errors actually reported in Example 2 (about 4.3e-8 for the trefoil holes, 2e-13 for the circular holes).

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We further assume that each hole $ D_j $ has a $ C^2 $ boundary, $ \partial D_j $.

issues.failure_explanation: The sentence is stated as a general fact and is used for the paper's domains, but under the standing Assumption assumption1 the holes have only C^2 boundaries. Elliptic boundary regularity lifts Steklov eigenfunctions only up to the regularity of the boundary (roughly C^{1,alpha} traces for C^2 boundaries); C^infty traces require C^infty boundaries. In the paper's own setting the claim {u_j|_{dO}} subset C^infty(dO) is therefore false as stated; only completeness/orthogonality in L^2 is justified at this regularity.

failure_location.quote:
restriction of the Steklov eigenfunctions to the boundary, 
$\{ u_j |_{\partial \Omega} \}_{j=0}^\infty \subset C^\infty(\partial \Omega)$, 
form a complete orthonormal basis of $L^2(\partial \Omega)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace C^infty by the regularity implied by C^2 boundaries (or additionally assume C^infty boundaries in Assumption assumption1); nothing else in the paper uses C^infty traces.
issues.overall_effect: A recalled regularity statement about the Steklov spectrum is false/unsupported for the C^2 domains the paper treats; no theorem or numerical guarantee otherwise relies on it.
issues.title: Boundary traces of Steklov eigenfunctions claimed C-infinity although the boundary is only assumed C^2
issues.why_classification: A local weakening of a recalled statement (or one added hypothesis) repairs it; no theorem, rate, or guarantee depends on C^infty boundary traces.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof derives D[phi](z) = Re[ integral with the oriented element d\xi = xi'(t)dt ]: the factor xi'(t)/|xi'(t)| = i*nu is exactly what converts the Cauchy kernel 1/(2*pi*i*(z-xi)) into the normal derivative of -log|z-xi| times arc length. Integrating the same kernel against |d\xi| (arc length), as the Definition (eqn: complex double layer) and the lemma's final formula do, removes this factor, so Re f_D[φ] is not D[φ] (e.g. for constant density on a circular hole the Gauss value 1/2 - |D_j|/b is only obtained with the oriented element), and the Sokhotski-Plemelj jump of item (2) fails for the arc-length version. Hence Lemma lem: Complex layer(1)-(2) are not proved for the operator as defined, and Lemma lem: properties double layer(4)-(5) and Lemma lem: characteristic(2) (used for the uniqueness part of Theorem thm: dirichlet) invoke them and are unsupported as written.

failure_location.quote: In fact, $\Re f_\mathcal{D}[\phi] = \mathcal{D}[\phi]$, which is a function on $\mathbb T_\tau\backslash\partial\Omega$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restore the oriented differential dξ in the Cauchy-type integral of \eqref{eqn: complex double layer} (and in the lemma's concluding formula), exactly as the proof's own computation uses; then all stated properties hold as proved and every downstream proof is valid unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma lem: Complex layer as stated is false for the constructed operator; the proofs of Lemma lem: properties double layer(4), Lemma lem: characteristic(2) and (via them) the uniqueness part of Theorem thm: dirichlet for M>=2 rest on it and fail as written.
issues.title: Complex double-layer potential integrated against |d\xi|; the derived representation and jump relation fail for the defined operator
issues.why_classification: A one-token definitional correction (|dξ| -> dξ), already forced by the paper's own computation, restores the intended construction; all subsequent proofs and results then hold as written, with no loss of substance.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Here, we used Green's identity, Lemma~\ref{lem: exact double layer}, and the condition $\sum_{j \in [M]} A_j = 0$, with $u(z)$ in~\eqref{e:uRep}.

issues.failure_explanation: The final step computes the flux of u across dD_j by applying Green's identity on D_j to the Omega-side trace: the displayed chain equates the integral of the exterior normal derivative of u with the interior Laplacian integral over D_j. Green's identity over D_j involves the D-side normal trace, while the quantity computed is the Omega-side derivative; these differ by the hypersingular jump of the double-layer potential, which the paper never establishes (only the value jump of Lemma lem: properties double layer(2) is proved, and one-sided normal derivatives of D[phi] for merely continuous phi are never shown to exist). Hence the final claim of Theorem thm: dirichlet, that A_j equals the flux across dD_j, is not established by the argument given. (The conclusion is true: the jump of d_nu D[phi] integrates to zero over each component, e.g. via the Cauchy-Riemann structure of the complex potential, so the two fluxes coincide and the D-side flux of the harmonic D[phi] vanishes.)
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the standard step: by the Cauchy-Riemann structure of f_D, the jump of the normal derivative satisfies ∫_{∂D_j}(∂_ν D[Ά]^+ - ∂_ν D[φ]^-) = -∮ ∂_σφ = 0 on each closed component, so the Omega-side flux equals the D-side flux, for which Green's identity gives 0 since D[φ] is harmonic in D_j.
issues.overall_effect: The flux-interpretation claim of Theorem thm: dirichlet (and the flux tables built on it in Section sec: dirichlet num) is not established by the written proof; existence, uniqueness and the representation formula are unaffected.
issues.title: Flux formula in Theorem thm: dirichlet justified by Green's identity across the boundary without the needed jump argument
issues.why_classification: A contained, standard argument using the paper's own complex-potential machinery restores the flux claim; no new proof architecture is needed and every other claim of the theorem stands.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Thus, we can uniquely choose $\phi_k$ satisfying $\mathcal{M}\phi = -\mathcal{M}\mathcal{S}[\psi_k](z_0)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proven characterization \eqref{e: steklov bie} has right-hand side σ S_0[φ_k] = σ(S[(I-M)φ_k] + Φ) with Φ = M[φ_k] a genuinely nonvanishing unknown: the proof of Theorem thm: steklov constructs the density with prescribed mean Mφ_k = -M[Sψ_k] ≠ 0 in general. The implemented pencil uses σ S(I-M)φ, i.e. it deletes the rank-one term σ(Mφ)͡ so the discretized equation reads (D*+I/2)ψ = σ Sψ for mean-zero ψ instead of σ(Sψ+Φ). These are different eigenproblems: taking the weighted boundary mean of the implemented equation forces M[Sψ]=0, whereas the Steklov correspondence requires Mφ_k = -M[Sψ_k]. In the continuum limit the implemented equation therefore captures only those Steklov eigenpairs whose canonical single-layer potential has zero boundary mean; that condition holds iff (D+I/2)^{-1}S1 is constant, which fails for generic (e.g. asymmetric, as in Example 5) domains, so eigenpairs are dropped. The appendix presents this system as the discrete analogue of \eqref{e: steklov bie} and the numerical guarantees of Examples 4-6 rest on that identification.

failure_location.quote:
We formulate the discrete eigenproblem, 
\[
(D_s + \onehalf I)(I - M) \vec{\phi} = \sigma S (I - M) \vec{\phi}. 
\]

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Discretize \eqref{e: steklov bie} as proved: replace the right-hand side by the discretization of S_0, i.e. add the rank-one term σ(Mφ)͡ to the pencil, ((D_s+I/2)(I-M))φ = σ(S(I-M)φ + (Mφ)͡), and re-run the experiments; alternatively, prove that the printed pencil has the Steklov spectrum, which the source does not attempt and which is false in general.
issues.overall_effect: The implemented Steklov algorithm of Appendix C is not the discretization of the proven equation \eqref{e: steklov bie}; as specified, it solves a restricted eigenproblem whose spectrum can be a proper subset of the Steklov spectrum, so the claimed computation of Steklov eigenpairs/eigenvalues (Examples 4-6) is unsupported by the paper's theory, and the reported agreements cannot be produced by the printed procedure.
issues.title: Discrete Steklov eigenproblem omits the constant term of the modified single-layer potential; implemented pencil is not the discretization of the proven equation
issues.why_classification: The repair is contained and mechanical (use the matrix of S_0 = S(I-M)+Φ, i.e. one rank-one term, and re-validate), preserving all theoretical guarantees; but the as-printed algorithm solves a different, restricted eigenproblem whose spectrum provably differs in general, so the defect exceeds a local typo while leaving the underlying theory intact.
